records.title: Postiz
records.summary: An open-source social media scheduler with a hosted cloud edition. The self-hosted edition posts through developer apps you register on each platform, and offers a public API, MCP and CLI.
records.why_it_matters: It is the self-hostable scheduler an agent can drive over MCP or its API, so one render can be queued to several platforms.
records.fit_notes: Self-hosting means your own app per platform: YouTube now publishes publicly without an audit, but TikTok leaves an own-account app private-only (see the TikTok guidelines record). The README states AGPL-3.0 for the self-hosted edition. The README's sponsor table advertises residential proxy IPs 'for social media'; that is a sponsor, not a Postiz feature, and proxy rotation is out of this hub's scope. The supported-platform list is drawn as images in the README and was not read. Not run here.

related.note: TikTok audit rules apply to the app you register.

claims.quote: You create your own developer apps on each platform and go through their approval (Meta, YouTube, TikTok can take weeks)

records.title: Mixpost
records.summary: A self-hosted social media scheduler built on Laravel. The free Lite edition is open source; Pro and Enterprise are paid one-time licences installed on your own server.
records.why_it_matters: It is a self-hosted alternative to Postiz, but the free edition does not post to YouTube, TikTok or Instagram.
records.fit_notes: Lite (free) publishes only to Facebook Pages, X and Mastodon per the pricing page; YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Threads, LinkedIn and Bluesky need Pro at $299 one-time (price read 2026-11-12). The README states MIT for this repository; paid editions are source-available and not for resale. No sentence on official API use was found in the README or the pricing page. No agent surface on the Lite README; the docs list API, CLI and MCP for paid editions, not read in depth. Not run here.

claims.quote: This repository contains the Lite version of Mixpost Pro, a commercial product product.
